title: Boolean conditions
outcome: Trace boolean conditions and explain the changed program before running it.
scenario: Two conditions for entry. A toy club accepts integer ages from 12 through 15 inclusive.
given: Python 3: age=15; allowed=(age>=12) and (age<=15); print(allowed). No type validation is implemented here.

steps.label: Combine with and
steps.detail: Both comparisons are True, so allowed is True.

explanation: A Boolean condition represents a yes-or-no result. And requires both conditions; checking only one boundary would accept values outside the intended interval.

counterfactual.reason: The lower condition remains True, but the upper condition fails.

student_task: Give both comparison results for ages 11, 15 and 16. Which comparison rejects each outside value, and why does and matter?
teacher_answer: Age 11 gives False/True, so False. Age 15 gives True/True, so True. Age 16 gives True/False, so False. Both interval boundaries must hold.
project_evidence: For Python readiness before the Responsible Plant Classifier, retain a trace of the values, the predicted outputs and the changed-case explanation. Use actual Python 3 results to check the prediction after reasoning first.
limits: This condition checks a declared numeric interval, not identity or authorisation; unexpected input types need separate handling.
review_note: Individually authored supported practice; distinct from the reserved independent case. Python semantics are checked on standalone snippets; no learned model or real pupil result is implied.
